# Remotes in GitHub

## Everything lives on one laptop

So far Bucky's whole menu — files and history — exists only on his computer.

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

That is fragile:

- If the laptop dies, the repo and its history are [gone]{.uwred}
- Bucky can't work on it from another machine
- He can't share it or collaborate with teammates

<div class="gap-md"></div>

The fix is a copy hosted online that we sync with. That is what [GitHub]{.uwred} is for.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## GitHub hosts your repo

[GitHub]{.uwred} is a website that stores Git repositories in the cloud. (GitLab and Bitbucket do the same thing.)

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

A hosted copy gives you three things:

- [Backup]{.uwred} — your work survives a dead laptop
- [Sync]{.uwred} — the same project on your laptop, your lab machine, a server
- [Collaboration]{.uwred} — teammates can see and contribute

<div class="gap-md"></div>

Remember: [Git]{.uwred} is the tool on your computer; [GitHub]{.uwred} is a place to host what Git tracks.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## SSH keys: how GitHub knows it's you

When you push work to GitHub, it has to be sure the push is really [from you]{.uwred}.

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

SSH keys are a matched pair:

- A [private key]{.uwred} that stays secret on your laptop
- A [public key]{.uwred} that you give to GitHub

<div class="gap-md"></div>

GitHub matches the two so you never type a password. You set this up [once per computer]{.uwred} — and you did it before class, so we will just confirm it works.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Verify your connection

Ask GitHub whether it recognizes your key:

```bash
ssh -T git@github.com
```

```
Hi buckybadger! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access.
```

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

That greeting means your key works and you're ready to push. If you instead get a [permission denied]{.uwred} error, follow the SSH setup guide or grab a neighbor before we go on.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Make a home for it on GitHub

In your browser, signed in to GitHub:

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

1. Click [+]{.uwred} (top right) → [New repository]{.uwred}
2. Name it [`gameday-menu`]{.uwred} to match the local folder
3. Leave it [Public]{.uwred}
4. [Do not]{.uwred} check "Add a README," ".gitignore," or a license
5. Click [Create repository]{.uwred}

<div class="gap-md"></div>

We skip the README and friends because we already have a repo with history. Starting a second history on GitHub would just collide with ours.

::: {.footer}
Starting a brand-new project instead? You can make the repo on GitHub first and clone it down — see the *Starting a Repo on GitHub* appendix.
:::


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Copy the SSH address

The new repo's page shows setup hints. Find the [SSH]{.uwred} address (make sure the SSH tab is selected, not HTTPS):

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

```
git@github.com:buckybadger/gameday-menu.git
```

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

This is the address of your GitHub copy. We will hand it to Git so your laptop knows where to send things.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Point your repo at GitHub: `git remote add`

A [remote]{.uwred} is a named connection to a hosted copy. Add one, using your own address:

```bash
git remote add origin git@github.com:buckybadger/gameday-menu.git
```

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

[`origin`]{.uwred} is the conventional name for your main remote. Confirm it:

```bash
git remote -v
```

```
origin	git@github.com:buckybadger/gameday-menu.git (fetch)
origin	git@github.com:buckybadger/gameday-menu.git (push)
```


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Send it up: `git push`

Push your `main` branch to the `origin` remote. The [`-u`]{.uwred} flag links your local `main` to the remote's `main`, so Git remembers the pairing:^[Prefer not to remember `-u`? Run `git config --global push.autoSetupRemote true` once per computer, and Git sets up the tracking link on your first bare `git push` automatically — no `-u` needed.]

```bash
git push -u origin main
```

```
Enumerating objects: 12, done.
Writing objects: 100% (12/12), 1.1 KiB | 1.1 MiB/s, done.
To github.com:buckybadger/gameday-menu.git
 * [new branch]      main -> main
branch 'main' set up to track 'origin/main'.
```

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

Reload the GitHub page: your files and every commit are now there. Note that `receipts/` and the `.tmp` files are [absent]{.uwred} — they were ignored, so they never traveled.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## The everyday loop: pull and push

Because that first push used [`-u`]{.uwred}, Git now knows the pairing — so syncing is just two short commands:

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

- [`git pull`]{.uwred} — bring down changes from GitHub (a teammate's work, or edits from another machine)
- [`git push`]{.uwred} — send your new commits up

<div class="gap-md"></div>

No need to name `origin main` again — the tracking link set up by `-u` fills that in. Good habit: [pull when you start]{.uwred}, [push when you finish]{.uwred}. And to get the repo onto a brand-new machine, [`git clone <address>`]{.uwred} creates the folder, sets up `origin`, and configures the same tracking automatically — so bare `git push`/`git pull` work there right away.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Your turn

::: {.callout-wide}
::: {.callout-important}
# Try it
Make a change and publish it:

1. Add a line to `desserts.txt` with `nano` (kringle, for the Wisconsin touch)
2. `git add` and `git commit` with a clear message
3. `git push` (no need for `origin main` now)
4. Refresh your repo on GitHub and watch the new commit appear
:::
:::


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Where we are

Bucky's menu now lives on GitHub, backed up and shareable:

- [`git remote add origin <address>`]{.uwred} links the local repo to GitHub
- [`git push -u origin main`]{.uwred} sends commits up the first time and sets up tracking; after that, bare [`git push`]{.uwred} and [`git pull`]{.uwred} are all you need
- [`git clone <address>`]{.uwred} copies a repo onto a new machine (tracking already set up)

<div class="gap-md"></div>

::: {.callout-wide}
